questions.question: ‘Queensberry rules’ is related to which of the following games:
questions.solution: **'Queensberry Rule'** is related to **Boxing**. These are the generally accepted rules in the sport of boxing. The name of the rule is so because the 9th Marquess of Queensberry endorsed this code.

questions.question: “The Champaran Satyagraha” took place in the year ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The **Champaran satyagraha** took place on 19 April **1917**__. Champaran is a district in the state of Bihar.
 
• Champaran satyagraha came into force because farmers were forced to grow indigo in a part of their land. This created much anger among farmers.
 
• In February **1919, the Rowlatt Act** was passed which allowed the British government to jail anyone suspected of plotting or overthrowing the government, without a trial. It is also known as the Black Act.
 
• In **1907, the Indian National Congress split** into extremists and moderates in the Surat session.
 
• In **1911**, King George V along with Queen Mary announced the **shifting of capital from Calcutta to Delhi**.

questions.question: National Human Rights Commission celebrated its silver jubilee on October 12, 2018, which was held in the city of:
questions.solution:
The **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)** celebrated its three day long **silver jubilee** on October 12, 2018 in **New Delhi**.

 
• It was concluded with ‘**Human Rights Walk**’ at Nehru Park.
 
• The Human Rights Walk was flagged off by NHRC Chairperson, **Justice H. L. Dattu** and sportspersons, **Boxer Mary Kom** and **Shooter Vijay Kumar.**
 
• The Human Rights Walk was organised to **build awareness on human rights** and seek people’s commitment to **promote and protect them**.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution is related to “Abolition of Untouchability”?
questions.solution:
• **Article 17 **in Part III of the Indian Constitution is a fundamental right which states that Untouchability is abolished and its practise in any form is a punishable offence.
 
• **Article 25 **of the Indian Constitution gives freedom of free profession, practise and propagation of religion.
 
• **Article 20 **of the Indian Constitution gives protection in respect of conviction of offences. When an individual or company is convicted of a crime, article 20 safeguards their rights.
 
• **Article 15 **of the Indian Constitution prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

questions.question: Sikkim became an Indian state in the year ________.
questions.solution:

questions.question: Hindon Elevated Road, India’s longest elevated road, was inaugurated in which city?
questions.solution:

questions.question: _________ is used to measure the force and velocity of wind.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Anemometer** __is a device used to measure the__ **force and velocity of the wind**__. It is also a common weather station instrument. It was invented by **Leon Battista Alberti** in the 15th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Lactometer** is a device used to measure the **density of milk,** or in layman's term, it is a device used to check the purity of milk. The more the density, purer is the milk. It was invented by **Mr. Dicas.**
 
• **Barometer **is a device used to measure **atmospheric pressure**. It also helps predict when the weather is likely to change. It was invented by **Evangelista Torricelli.**
 
• **Milometer** is a device attached to the wheels of the vehicle which is used to **measure the distance traveled** by the vehicle. It was invented by **Thomas Savery **for ships.

questions.question: The word’s longest sandstone cave named Krem Puri was discovered in which North-eastern state?
questions.solution:
• **Krem Puri**, the world’s longest sandstone caves were discovered near Laitsohum village in Mawsynram area in **East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya.**
 
• The cave is **24,583 metres (24.5 km)** in length and is known for its **complex cave systems** hidden under its undulating hills.
 
• It was discovered in 2016 but its actual length was found during an expedition to measure and map it by Meghalaya Adventurers’ Association (MAA).

questions.question: Which two words were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42ⁿd Amendment in 1976?
questions.solution:
**Socialist and secular** are the two words added to the Indian constitution by the **42nd amendment**.

**42nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1976, **was enacted during the Emergency (25 June 1975 – 21 March 1977) by the Indian National Congress government headed by Indira Gandhi. This amendment brought about the most widespread changes to the Constitution in its history, and is sometimes called a **“Mini-Constitution”**. Few important amendments are:

 
• Added Fundamental Duties by the citizens (new Part IV A).
 
• Four Directive Principles were added viz. Article 39, Article 39A, Article 43A and Article 48A, and were given precedence over fundamental rights.
 
• It made the power of parliament supreme.

questions.question: Humayun was defeated by Shear Shah Suri in the battle of Kannauj in the year ________.
questions.solution:
The **Battle of Kanauj** was fought in the year** __1540__** in which Humayun was defeated by Sher Shah Suri. This battle ended the Mughal Empire. Humayun managed to run away from the battle and for the next 15 years, he lived like a wanderer.

Just before the battle of Kanauj, **Battle of Chausa** was fought in **1539** between Humayun and Sher Shah Suri in which Sher Shah Suri gained Victory.

questions.question: _________ is used commercially in the preparation of jellies, jams and marmalades because of its ability to form a thick gel like solution.
questions.solution:
**Pectins** are carbohydrate polymers found in plants where it contributes to cell structure. It is also usually found in **apples, berries and other fruits.** When pectin is heated with sugar, it starts developing the characteristics of thick gel like solution as in jams and jellies.

**Glucose** is a simple sugar and is mainly made by plants and most algae during photosynthesis. It is a type of sweet which we get from the food we eat and this sweet is used by the body and is converted into energy.

**Lactose** is a compound composed of glucose and galactose. It is water soluble and has a **mildly sweet **taste. It is majorly used in the food industry.

**Maltose** also known as maltobiose or malt sugar is a carbohydrate formed from two units of glucose. It is found in **wheat, barley and other grains**. It is also used to add **natural sweetness** to different breakfast cereals.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an important site of the Indus Valley civilisation?
questions.solution:
**Dibrugarh** is not an important site of Indus Valley Civilisation.

**Lothal** was one of the southernmost city of Indus Valley Civilisation. It has the world's oldest known ports.

**Mohenjodaro** and **Harappa** was one of the largest settlements of the Indus Valley civilisation and one of the world’s earliest major cities. They were known for their impressive and organised layout.
